title: The spherical light wave in the moving system
spoken: The moving x component squared plus the moving y component squared plus the moving z component squared equals c squared times the moving time squared.
explanation: The admitted scaled coordinate map carries the stationary spherical light wave into this moving-frame wave equation. The exact cancellation leaves the common scale arbitrary. It checks compatibility conditional on the map and the light-wave premise; it does not derive the map or fix its normalization.
assumptions: The moving frame uses xi = phi gamma (x - vt), eta = phi y, zeta = phi z and tau = phi gamma (t - vx/c squared), with gamma = 1/sqrt(1 - v squared/c squared).
The coordinates and speeds are real, c > 0 and |v| < c; the common scale phi(v) is finite and nonzero.
A pulse emitted at the common zero event has stationary-frame wave-front coordinates satisfying x squared + y squared + z squared = c squared t squared.
Modern teaching notation. Component labels x, y and z distinguish the three moving spatial coordinates; the source writes xi, eta, zeta, tau and V.

notes.title: The moving-frame wave condition
notes.explanation: For events on this emitted light wave, the moving-frame squared spatial distance from the common origin equals c squared times the moving coordinate time squared.

notes.title: Squared spatial distance
notes.explanation: Add the squared x, y and z components to describe the spherical front in the moving system.

notes.title: The longitudinal component squared
notes.explanation: Square the coordinate along the relative motion; its mixed space-time terms cancel against those in the time contribution.

notes.title: The first sideways component squared
notes.explanation: The y contribution carries the same common scale squared as the other three coordinates.

notes.title: The second sideways component squared
notes.explanation: The z contribution completes the three-dimensional spherical wave condition.

notes.title: The light-travel distance squared
notes.explanation: Multiply the square of the speed of light by the square of the moving coordinate time to obtain the squared radius. This relation also holds when the common scale is negative.

notes.title: The same light speed
notes.explanation: This is the positive speed c admitted in the stationary light-wave condition. The cancellation checks the same value in the moving coordinates.

notes.title: Moving coordinate time squared
notes.explanation: The elapsed time is assigned by synchronized clocks at rest in the moving frame.

notes.title: Moving longitudinal coordinate
notes.explanation: The x component of the event's position in the moving frame, called xi in the source.

notes.title: Moving y coordinate
notes.explanation: The y component of the same moving-frame position, called eta in the source. The subscript identifies the component.

notes.title: Moving z coordinate
notes.explanation: The z component of the same moving-frame position, called zeta in the source. The subscript identifies the component.

notes.title: Speed of light
notes.explanation: The positive c of modern notation is the source's V.

notes.title: Moving coordinate time
notes.explanation: The time coordinate of the event in the moving frame, called tau in the source. It is not the proper time recorded along one clock's path.
